records.source: צַדִּ֤יק אַתָּה֙ יְהוָ֔ה כִּ֥י אָרִ֖יב אֵלֶ֑יךָ אַ֤ךְ מִשְׁפָּטִים֙ אֲדַבֵּ֣ר אוֹתָ֔ךְ מַדּ֗וּעַ דֶּ֤רֶךְ רְשָׁעִים֙ צָלֵ֔חָה שָׁל֖וּ כָּל־בֹּ֥גְדֵי בָֽגֶד׃
records.gloss: Righteous [are] you, Yahweh, when I bring a case to you; yet judgments I will speak with you: why [does the] way of wicked [ones] prosper, [why] are at ease all [who] betray [with] betrayal?
pieces: You are in the right, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, whenever I bring a case against {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}; \q still, I must set my charges before {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}: \q Why does the way of the wicked succeed? \q Why do all the faithless live untroubled?

L.1: Righteous [are] {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, when I bring a case to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}; \q yet I will speak judgments with {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}: \q Why does [the] way of [the] wicked prosper? \q [Why] are all who betray [with] betrayal at ease?

R.1: {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are righteous; when I argue with {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are always in the right. \q But I still want to ask {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} about what is fair. \q Why do wicked people do so well? \q Why do people who are never loyal to anyone live without a care?

decisions.choice: Jeremiah's prayer goes on from 11:18-23
decisions.reason: The chapter division falls in the middle of one of Jeremiah's prayers to God, which began at 11:18. He has just learned of the plot against his life by the people of his home town (11:21-23); now he turns to the larger question it raises. God answers in verses 5-6.

decisions.choice: righteous ... bring a case ... judgments: the language of a court
decisions.reason: "Righteous" here is the word for the party who is in the right in a lawsuit. The verb is the one used for bringing a legal complaint, and "judgments" are the points of a case. Jeremiah grants at the start that God will be found in the right, yet he still wants to argue his complaint (compare Job 23:3-7; Habakkuk 1:2-4, 13).

decisions.choice: all who betray with betrayal: people utterly treacherous
decisions.reason: The verb and its noun from the same root are set side by side for emphasis: people whose whole way of life is breaking faith. The same verb returns in verse 6 for Jeremiah's own family.

decisions.choice: You are in the right ... set my charges before you
decisions.reason: Balanced keeps the court picture: "in the right" is what "righteous" means in a lawsuit, and "charges" are what Jeremiah wants to argue.

decisions.choice: argue with you ... what is fair ... never loyal to anyone
decisions.reason: Readable keeps "righteous" and then says plainly what a court case means; "never loyal to anyone" explains the doubled word for betrayal.

records.heading: Why does the way of the wicked succeed?

records.source: נְטַעְתָּם֙ גַּם־שֹׁרָ֔שׁוּ יֵלְכ֖וּ גַּם־עָ֣שׂוּ פֶ֑רִי קָר֤וֹב אַתָּה֙ בְּפִיהֶ֔ם וְרָח֖וֹק מִכִּלְיוֹתֵיהֶֽם׃
records.gloss: You planted them, also they have taken root; they go, also they have made fruit; near [are] you in their mouth and far from their kidneys.
pieces: You planted them, and they have taken root; \q they flourish and bear fruit. \q You are near in their mouths \q but far from their inmost being.

L.2: You planted them; they have even taken root; \q they go on; they even produce fruit. \q Near [are] {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} in their mouth, \q and far from their kidneys.

R.2: You planted them, and they put down roots. \q They grow and produce fruit. \q They talk about {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} all the time, \q but deep inside they do not care about {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} at all.

decisions.choice: planted ... taken root ... fruit: the wicked pictured as a thriving plant
decisions.reason: Jeremiah's complaint is that God himself planted these people and lets them grow. God had used the same picture of Israel, planted as a choice vine (2:21; 11:16-17).

decisions.choice: near in their mouth, far from their kidneys: they speak of God but do not hold him inwardly
decisions.reason: The kidneys were thought of as the seat of a person's deepest feelings and motives, often paired with the heart (11:20; 17:10; Psalm 7:10). God's name is always on their lips, but he has no place in their inner life (compare Isaiah 29:13).

decisions.choice: inmost being (Balanced); deep inside (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the sense of "kidneys" rather than the body part, which would puzzle a modern reader. Literal keeps the word.

decisions.choice: They talk about you all the time
decisions.reason: Readable explains the idiom "near in their mouth": God is often in their talk.

records.source: וְאַתָּ֤ה יְהוָה֙ יְדַעְתָּ֔נִי תִּרְאֵ֕נִי וּבָחַנְתָּ֥ לִבִּ֖י אִתָּ֑ךְ הַתִּקֵם֙ כְּצֹ֣אן לְטִבְחָ֔ה וְהַקְדִּשֵׁ֖ם לְי֥וֹם הֲרֵגָֽה׃ס
records.gloss: And you, Yahweh, you know me; you see me, and you test my heart with you; drag them off like sheep for slaughter, and set them apart for [a] day of killing.
pieces: But {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, know me; {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} see me \q and test how my heart stands toward {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}. \q Drag them away like sheep to be slaughtered; \q set them apart for the day of killing.

L.3: And {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} know me; {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} see me, \q and {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} test my heart [toward] {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}. \q Drag them off like sheep for slaughter, \q and set them apart for [the] day of killing.

R.3: But {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} know me, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}. You see me. \q You test my heart and see how I feel about {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}. \q Drag those wicked people away like sheep to be killed. \q Set them aside for the day when they will be slaughtered.

decisions.choice: test my heart: examine it as metal is tested
decisions.reason: The verb is used for testing metal to find out what it is made of. Jeremiah appeals to God, who has examined his heart and knows it is loyal to him, unlike the people of verse 2 (11:20; 17:10; 20:12).

decisions.choice: sheep for slaughter ... set apart: Jeremiah's own words turned on his enemies
decisions.reason: In 11:19 Jeremiah said he had been like a trusting lamb led to the slaughter. Now he asks that his enemies meet that fate. "Set apart" is the word for making something holy, used of setting animals apart for sacrifice; here it is used with bitter irony for marking the wicked out for death (compare 6:4; 22:7).

decisions.choice: a prayer for judgment, left to God
decisions.reason: Like some psalms (Psalm 109; 137:7-9), Jeremiah asks God to punish his enemies; he does not take revenge himself but leaves the case with God (11:20).

decisions.choice: those wicked people
decisions.reason: Readable names who "them" are, from verses 1-2.

records.source: עַד־מָתַי֙ תֶּאֱבַ֣ל הָאָ֔רֶץ וְעֵ֥שֶׂב כָּל־הַשָּׂדֶ֖ה יִיבָ֑שׁ מֵרָעַ֣ת יֹֽשְׁבֵי־בָ֗הּ סָפְתָ֤ה בְהֵמוֹת֙ וָע֔וֹף כִּ֣י אָמְר֔וּ לֹ֥א יִרְאֶ֖ה אֶת־אַחֲרִיתֵֽנוּ׃
records.gloss: Until when will mourn the land, and [the] grass of every field wither? From [the] evil of [those] dwelling in it are swept away animals and bird[s], for they have said, he will not see our end.
pieces: How long will the land mourn \q and the plants of every field dry up? \q Because of the evil of those who live in it, \q animals and birds have perished, \q for the people say, "He will not see what becomes of us."

L.4: Until when will the land mourn, \q and the grass of every field wither? \q Because of [the] evil of those dwelling in it, \q animals and birds are swept away, \q for they have said, "He will not see our end."

R.4: How long will the land be dry and full of sorrow? \q How long will the grass in the fields be dead? \q The animals and birds have died \q because the people who live in the land are evil. \q They say, "He will not see what happens to us in the end."

decisions.choice: mourn, with drying up in view
decisions.reason: The verb usually means to mourn, and the land is pictured as grieving (12:11; 23:10; Isaiah 24:4; Hosea 4:3). A word spelled the same way means to dry up, which fits the withered grass in the next line, and both senses may be heard together.

decisions.choice: the land and its creatures suffer for the people's evil
decisions.reason: Drought and the death of animals are among the covenant curses (Deuteronomy 28:23-24). The people's sin brings harm on the whole land (compare 3:3; 14:1-6; Hosea 4:1-3).

decisions.choice: he will not see our end: who "he" is is left open
alternatives: God will not see our end
the prophet will not live to see our end
decisions.reason: The speakers may mean God: he does not see or care what happens to us. Or they may mean Jeremiah: he will not live to see the ruin he predicts. The Greek translation reads "God will not see our ways". The Hebrew does not say which.

decisions.choice: two "How long" questions; "dry and full of sorrow"
decisions.reason: Readable repeats "How long" for each half of the question and puts both senses of the first verb (see m1) into plain words.

records.source: כִּ֣י אֶת־רַגְלִ֥ים׀רַ֨צְתָּה֙ וַיַּלְא֔וּךָ וְאֵ֥יךְ תְּתַֽחֲרֶ֖ה אֶת־הַסּוּסִ֑ים וּבְאֶ֤רֶץ שָׁלוֹם֙ אַתָּ֣ה בוֹטֵ֔חַ וְאֵ֥יךְ תַּעֲשֶׂ֖ה בִּגְא֥וֹן הַיַּרְדֵּֽן׃
records.gloss: For with [men] on foot you have run, and they have wearied you, and how will you compete with the horses? And in [a] land of peace you [are] secure, and how will you do in [the] thicket of the Jordan?
pieces: If you have raced with runners on foot and they have worn you out, \q how will you keep pace with horses? \q If you feel secure only in a peaceful land, \q what will you do in the thick brush along the Jordan?

L.5: If you have run with [men] on foot and they have wearied you, \q then how will you compete with horses? \q And [if] in a land of peace you [are] secure, \q then how will you do in the thicket of the Jordan?

R.5: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} answered me: If you get tired racing against people on foot, \q how will you race against horses? \q If you feel safe only where there is peace, \q what will you do in the thick bushes along the Jordan River, where lions live?

decisions.choice: God answers Jeremiah
decisions.reason: Nothing in the Hebrew marks the change of speaker, but the "you" is now Jeremiah, and God replies to his complaint not with an explanation but with a warning that harder trials are coming.

decisions.choice: racing men on foot, then horses: if small troubles tire you, worse ones are ahead
decisions.reason: The picture is of a footrace. If Jeremiah is worn out by the plots so far, how will he cope with greater danger? Verse 6 names the first of it: his own family.

decisions.choice: you are secure
decisions.reason: The usual sense of the word is to trust or feel safe: if Jeremiah can feel safe only in quiet country, how will he manage in the wild? A rarer word spelled the same way means to fall down, which would give "if you stumble in a safe land". The sense of the whole saying is the same either way.

decisions.choice: the thicket of the Jordan: the dense growth along the river, where lions lived
decisions.reason: The phrase is literally "the pride of the Jordan": the thick growth of trees and reeds along the river valley. It was wild country where lions had their lairs (49:19; 50:44; Zechariah 11:3).

decisions.choice: The LORD answered me ... the Jordan River, where lions live
decisions.reason: Readable names the speaker, which the Hebrew leaves to the reader (see m1), and says why the Jordan thicket was dangerous (see m4).

records.source: כִּ֧י גַם־אַחֶ֣יךָ וּבֵית־אָבִ֗יךָ גַּם־הֵ֨מָּה֙ בָּ֣גְדוּ בָ֔ךְ גַּם־הֵ֛מָּה קָרְא֥וּ אַחֲרֶ֖יךָ מָלֵ֑א אַל־תַּאֲמֵ֣ן בָּ֔ם כִּֽי־יְדַבְּר֥וּ אֵלֶ֖יךָ טוֹבֽוֹת׃ס
records.gloss: For even your brothers and [the] house of your father, even they have dealt treacherously with you; even they have called after you full; do not believe them, though they speak to you good [things].
pieces: Your brothers too, the household of your own father, \q even they have broken faith with you; \q they too have raised a loud outcry against you. \q Do not believe them, though they speak kindly to you.

L.6: For even your brothers and the house of your father, \q even they have dealt treacherously with you; \q even they have called after you [with a] full [voice]. \q Do not trust them, though they speak good [words] to you.

R.6: Even your brothers and the rest of your family \q have turned against you. \q They too are shouting against you. \q Do not trust them, even when they say nice things to you.

decisions.choice: your brothers and your father's house: Jeremiah's own family
decisions.reason: Jeremiah came from a priestly family of Anathoth (1:1), and the men of Anathoth had plotted to kill him (11:21-23). Now God tells him that even his close relatives are part of it. "Dealt treacherously" is the word used of the wicked in verse 1.

decisions.choice: they have called after you in full: they have raised a loud outcry against you
alternatives: they have gathered a crowd against you
decisions.reason: The exact sense of "full" here is unclear. It may mean that they shout loudly after him, or that they have called a full crowd together against him (compare 4:5, where the same word means "aloud").

decisions.choice: the rest of your family
decisions.reason: Readable puts "the house of your father" as "family", which is what the phrase means.

records.source: עָזַ֨בְתִּי֙ אֶת־בֵּיתִ֔י נָטַ֖שְׁתִּי אֶת־נַחֲלָתִ֑י נָתַ֛תִּי אֶת־יְדִד֥וּת נַפְשִׁ֖י בְּכַ֥ף אֹיְבֶֽיהָ׃
records.gloss: I have forsaken my house; I have abandoned my inheritance; I have given [the] beloved of my soul into [the] palm of her enemies.
pieces: I have left {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} house; \q I have cast off {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} inheritance. \q I have handed the one I love with all {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} heart over to her enemies.

L.7: I have forsaken {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} house; \q I have abandoned {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} inheritance; \q I have given the beloved of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} soul into [the] palm of her enemies.

R.7: I have left {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} house. \q I have turned away from the people who belong to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. \q I have handed the people I love so much over to their enemies.

decisions.choice: God speaks of his own people
decisions.reason: From here to verse 13 God himself laments what he has had to do. The verbs are in the past tense, as if the judgment had already happened, though it was still to come.

decisions.choice: my house ... my inheritance: God's people and land
decisions.reason: "House" may be the temple or, as often, the household of God's people; here it stands beside "inheritance", the people and land that belong to God as his own possession (2:7; 10:16; Deuteronomy 32:9).

decisions.choice: the beloved of my soul ... into the palm: the one I dearly love, into the power of
decisions.reason: "Soul" here means God's own self: the one he loves with all his being. "Into the palm of" means into someone's power. The people are pictured as a beloved woman, so "her enemies".

decisions.choice: the people who belong to me ... the people I love ... their enemies
decisions.reason: Readable explains "inheritance" and "beloved" as the people, and so says "their" for "her".

records.heading: I have left my house

records.source: הָיְתָה־לִּ֥י נַחֲלָתִ֖י כְּאַרְיֵ֣ה בַיָּ֑עַר נָתְנָ֥ה עָלַ֛י בְּקוֹלָ֖הּ עַל־כֵּ֥ן שְׂנֵאתִֽיהָ׃
records.gloss: Has become to me my inheritance like a lion in the forest; she has given against me with her voice; therefore I hate her.
pieces: My inheritance has turned on {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} like a lion in the forest; \q she roars against {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, and so I have come to hate her.

L.8: My inheritance has become to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} like a lion in the forest; \q she has raised her voice against {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}; therefore I hate her.

R.8: The people who belong to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} have turned against {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} like a lion in the forest. \q They roar at {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. So now I hate them.

decisions.choice: like a lion ... gave her voice against me: the people roar at God like a hostile lion
decisions.reason: "To give the voice" is used of a lion roaring (2:15). The people God treasured have turned on him as a wild beast turns on a keeper.

decisions.choice: hate: reject, turn away from
decisions.reason: In covenant language "hate" can mean to reject or refuse to favor, set against "love" as choosing (Malachi 1:2-3; Hosea 9:15). God is not saying he has stopped caring (verse 7 still calls her "beloved"), but that he has withdrawn his protection.

decisions.choice: the people who belong to me ... them
decisions.reason: As in verse 7, Readable explains "my inheritance" as the people.

records.source: הַעַ֨יִט צָב֤וּעַ נַחֲלָתִי֙ לִ֔י הַעַ֖יִט סָבִ֣יב עָלֶ֑יהָ לְכ֗וּ אִסְפ֛וּ כָּל־חַיַּ֥ת הַשָּׂדֶ֖ה הֵתָ֥יוּ לְאָכְלָֽה׃
records.gloss: [Is] a speckled bird of prey my inheritance to me? [Are] birds of prey all around against her? Go, gather every animal of the field; bring [them] to devour.
pieces: Has {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} inheritance become to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} a speckled bird of prey, \q set upon by birds of prey on every side? \q Go, gather all the wild animals; bring them to eat.

L.9: [Is] {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} inheritance to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} a speckled bird of prey? \q [Are] birds of prey all around against her? \q Go, gather every animal of the field; bring [them] to devour.

R.9: The people who belong to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} are like a bird with spotted feathers, \q and the other wild birds are all around it, attacking it. \q Go and gather all the wild animals. Bring them to eat.

decisions.choice: a speckled bird of prey
decisions.reason: The word rendered "speckled" (or "colored") is found only here. The picture seems to be of a bird with odd markings that the other birds of prey gang up on. The same letters can be read as "hyena", and the Greek translation speaks of a hyena's den; then the line would be "Is my inheritance a hyena's lair to me?"

decisions.choice: the questions expect the answer yes
decisions.reason: Both questions are of the kind that state something: God's people have become like a prey bird mobbed by others. The commands that follow call the wild animals to join the attack (compare Isaiah 56:9; Ezekiel 39:17).

decisions.choice: go, gather ... bring: commands to unnamed hearers
decisions.reason: The plural commands are not addressed to anyone named; they may be to the enemies of verse 7 or simply a call for the wild animals to come. Either way, the nations are pictured as beasts gathering to feed.

decisions.choice: questions turned into statements
decisions.reason: Readable says plainly what the questions mean (see m2).

records.source: רֹעִ֤ים רַבִּים֙ שִֽׁחֲת֣וּ כַרְמִ֔י בֹּסְס֖וּ אֶת־חֶלְקָתִ֑י נָֽתְנ֛וּ אֶת־חֶלְקַ֥ת חֶמְדָּתִ֖י לְמִדְבַּ֥ר שְׁמָמָֽה׃
records.gloss: Shepherds many have ruined my vineyard; they have trampled my portion; they have made [the] portion of my delight into [a] wilderness of desolation.
pieces: Many shepherds have wrecked {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} vineyard \q and trampled down {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} field; \q they have turned the field I delight in into an empty wilderness.

L.10: Many shepherds have ruined {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} vineyard; \q they have trampled {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} portion; \q they have made {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} delightful portion into a wilderness of desolation.

R.10: Many rulers have ruined {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} vineyard \q and trampled {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} field. \q They have turned {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} lovely field into an empty desert.

decisions.choice: many shepherds: rulers, here probably foreign kings and their armies
decisions.reason: "Shepherds" is a common picture for rulers (2:8; 23:1-4). In 6:3 shepherds with their flocks are enemy commanders camped around Jerusalem, and that fits here: invading kings who let their armies graze the land bare. Judah's own leaders are also called shepherds who ruined the flock (10:21; 23:1).

decisions.choice: my vineyard ... my portion: God's people and land
decisions.reason: Israel is God's vineyard in Isaiah 5:1-7 and Jeremiah 2:21. "Portion" is a plot of land, and the land is God's own share (Deuteronomy 32:9). "The portion of my delight" is the land God treasured (3:19).

decisions.choice: rulers
decisions.reason: Readable gives the meaning of the picture "shepherds" (see m1) and keeps the vineyard picture, which explains itself.

records.source: שָׂמָהּ֙ לִשְׁמָמָ֔ה אָבְלָ֥ה עָלַ֖י שְׁמֵמָ֑ה נָשַׁ֨מָּה֙ כָּל־הָאָ֔רֶץ כִּ֛י אֵ֥ין אִ֖ישׁ שָׂ֥ם עַל־לֵֽב׃
records.gloss: He has made it into [a] desolation; it mourns to me, desolate; desolate [is] all the land, for there is no man laying [it] on heart.
pieces: It has been made a desolation; \q ruined, it mourns before {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. \q The whole land lies desolate, \q because no one takes it to heart.

L.11: One has made it a desolation; \q it mourns to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, desolate. \q The whole land has been made desolate, \q for there is no one laying [it] to heart.

R.11: The rulers have turned it into an empty waste. \q It lies ruined and cries to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} in sorrow. \q The whole land has been ruined, \q but no one cares.

decisions.choice: he has made it: the doer is left general
decisions.reason: The verb has "he" as its subject without naming him. It most likely refers back to the shepherds of verse 10 as a group, or is used in a general way: "it has been made".

decisions.choice: desolation ... desolate ... made desolate: one root repeated
decisions.reason: Three words from the same root follow each other, hammering home the emptiness of the land. The land mourns (as in verse 4) while its people do not.

decisions.choice: laying it on heart: caring, paying attention
decisions.reason: To "put on the heart" means to give something serious thought and let it move you (Isaiah 42:25; 57:1).

decisions.choice: The rulers
decisions.reason: Readable names the subject from verse 10 (see m1).

records.source: עַֽל־כָּל־שְׁפָיִ֣ם בַּמִּדְבָּ֗ר בָּ֚אוּ שֹֽׁדְדִ֔ים כִּ֣י חֶ֤רֶב לַֽיהוָה֙ אֹֽכְלָ֔ה מִקְצֵה־אֶ֖רֶץ וְעַד־קְצֵ֣ה הָאָ֑רֶץ אֵ֥ין שָׁל֖וֹם לְכָל־בָּשָֽׂר׃ס
records.gloss: Upon all [the] bare heights in the wilderness have come destroyers, for [the] sword of Yahweh devours from [the] end of [the] land and to [the] end of the land; there is no peace for any flesh.
pieces: Destroyers have swept over all the bare hills in the wilderness, \q for the sword of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} is eating its way from one end of the land to the other; \q no living thing has peace.

L.12: Upon all [the] bare heights in the wilderness destroyers have come, \q for [the] sword of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} devours from [one] end of the land to [the other] end of the land; \q there is no peace for any flesh.

R.12: Destroying armies have come over all the bare hills in the desert. \q The sword of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} is killing people from one end of the land to the other. \q No one has any peace.

decisions.choice: bare heights: open hilltops, the routes invaders came by
decisions.reason: The word means windswept, bare hills (3:2, 21; 4:11). Destruction comes over the high ground into the land.

decisions.choice: the sword of the LORD devours: the invaders are God's instrument
decisions.reason: The armies are not acting on their own; it is God's sword that "eats" through the land (47:6; Deuteronomy 32:42). The speaker may be God speaking of himself by name, or the prophet taking up God's lament.

decisions.choice: the land: Judah, not the whole earth
decisions.reason: The same word can mean "land" or "earth". The context is the ruin of God's own land (verses 10-11), so the land of Judah is meant.

decisions.choice: no peace for any flesh: no living being is safe
decisions.reason: "All flesh" means every living creature, people above all. "Peace" here is safety and well-being.

decisions.choice: Destroying armies ... is killing people
decisions.reason: Readable says who the destroyers are and what the sword's "devouring" means.

records.source: זָרְע֤וּ חִטִּים֙ וְקֹצִ֣ים קָצָ֔רוּ נֶחְל֖וּ לֹ֣א יוֹעִ֑לוּ וּבֹ֨שׁוּ֙ מִתְּבוּאֹ֣תֵיכֶ֔ם מֵחֲר֖וֹן אַף־יְהוָֽה׃ס
records.gloss: They have sown wheat and thorns they have reaped; they have exhausted themselves, they do not profit; and be ashamed of your harvests from [the] burning of [the] anger of Yahweh.
pieces: They sowed wheat but reaped thorns; \q they wore themselves out for nothing. \q Be ashamed of your harvests, \q because of the fierce anger of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

L.13: They have sown wheat, and thorns they have reaped; \q they have worn themselves out; they gain nothing. \q So be ashamed of your harvests \q because of the burning anger of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

R.13: The people planted wheat, but they gathered only thorns. \q They worked until they were exhausted, but they gained nothing. \q So be ashamed of your harvests, \q because {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} is burning with anger.

decisions.choice: sowing wheat and reaping thorns: all their work comes to nothing
decisions.reason: It may describe the failed harvests of a ruined land, or be a saying about effort that ends in loss (compare Leviticus 26:20; Deuteronomy 28:38; Hosea 8:7; Micah 6:15).

decisions.choice: be ashamed of your harvests
alternatives: they will be ashamed of their harvests
decisions.reason: The form of the verb can be a command, "be ashamed", or a statement, "they are ashamed". "Your harvests" fits a command spoken directly to the people. Some read "they are ashamed of their harvests", keeping the third person of the first half; the sense is the same: disgrace at a failed harvest.

decisions.choice: the burning of the anger: fierce anger
decisions.reason: The phrase pairs a word for burning with the word for anger (literally "nose"), a common way of saying God's anger is fierce (4:8, 26; 25:37).

decisions.choice: The people
decisions.reason: Readable names the subject, the people of the land.

records.source: כֹּ֣ה׀אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֗ה עַל־כָּל־שְׁכֵנַי֙ הָֽרָעִ֔ים הַנֹּֽגְעִים֙ בַּֽנַּחֲלָ֔ה אֲשֶׁר־הִנְחַ֥לְתִּי אֶת־עַמִּ֖י אֶת־יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל הִנְנִ֤י נֹֽתְשָׁם֙ מֵעַ֣ל אַדְמָתָ֔ם וְאֶת־בֵּ֥ית יְהוּדָ֖ה אֶתּ֥וֹשׁ מִתּוֹכָֽם׃
records.gloss: Thus says Yahweh concerning all my neighbors, the evil [ones], who touch the inheritance which I caused to inherit my people Israel: here I [am] uprooting them from upon their land, and the house of Judah I will uproot from their midst.
pieces: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} says this concerning all {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} wicked neighbors who lay hands on the inheritance I gave {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people Israel to possess: Look, I am going to uproot them from their own soil, and the house of Judah I will uproot from their midst.

L.14: Thus says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} concerning all {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} evil neighbors who touch the inheritance that I gave {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people Israel to inherit: Look, I am uprooting them from their land, and the house of Judah I will uproot from among them.

R.14: This is what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} says about all the wicked nations around Israel: They are {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} neighbors, and they have attacked the land I gave {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people Israel as their own. Now I am going to uproot those nations from their land. And I will uproot the people of Judah from among them.

decisions.choice: my evil neighbors: the nations around Israel
decisions.reason: The neighbors are the peoples on Judah's borders, such as Edom, Moab, Ammon and the Philistines, who raided the land and took part of it when Judah was weak (2 Kings 24:2; Ezekiel 25; 35). God calls them his own neighbors because the land is his.

decisions.choice: touch the inheritance: lay hands on it, seize or attack it
decisions.reason: The verb "touch" is used of harming or seizing (Genesis 26:11; Zechariah 2:12).

decisions.choice: uproot ... uproot: one verb for judgment and for rescue
decisions.reason: This is the first of the verbs of Jeremiah's call, "to uproot and to tear down" (1:10). The nations will be uprooted from their land in judgment, while Judah will be uprooted from among the nations where it has been taken, to be brought home. The same word is used for both.

decisions.choice: the change from prose to oracle
decisions.reason: Verses 14-17 are prose, not poetry. They widen God's lament over his own land (verses 7-13) to a promise about the nations around it.

decisions.choice: Look
decisions.reason: The Hebrew word that draws attention to what follows is "Look" at Literal and Balanced; Readable puts it as "Now".

decisions.choice: a long sentence split, and "neighbors" explained as nations
decisions.reason: Readable breaks the sentence into short ones and says who the neighbors are (see m1).

records.heading: Uprooted and brought back

records.source: וְהָיָ֗ה אַֽחֲרֵי֙ נָתְשִׁ֣י אוֹתָ֔ם אָשׁ֖וּב וְרִֽחַמְתִּ֑ים וַהֲשִׁבֹתִ֛ים אִ֥ישׁ לְנַחֲלָת֖וֹ וְאִ֥ישׁ לְאַרְצֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: And it will be, after my uprooting them, I will return and have compassion on them, and I will bring them back, each to his inheritance and each to his land.
pieces: But after I have uprooted them, I will again have compassion on them, and I will bring them back, {{gender:each one to their own|each man to his own}} inheritance and {{gender:each one to their own|each man to his own}} land.

L.15: And it will be, after I have uprooted them, I will turn back and have compassion on them, and I will bring them back, {{gender:each one to their|each man to his}} inheritance and {{gender:each one to their|each man to his}} land.

R.15: But after I have uprooted them, I will feel sorry for them again. I will bring them all back to their own property and their own land.

decisions.choice: them: the neighboring nations
decisions.reason: The "them" who are uprooted, pitied and brought back are the neighbors of verse 14. God's compassion reaches even the nations that harmed his people (compare 48:47; 49:6, 39).

decisions.choice: I will return and have compassion: I will again have compassion
decisions.reason: "Return" before another verb often means doing the thing again. God will turn from judgment back to mercy.

decisions.choice: feel sorry for them ... their own property
decisions.reason: Readable says "feel sorry for" for compassion and "property" for inheritance, the land each family held.

records.source: וְהָיָ֡ה אִם־לָמֹ֣ד יִלְמְדוּ֩ אֶת־דַּֽרְכֵ֨י עַמִּ֜י לְהִשָּׁבֵ֤עַ בִּשְׁמִי֙ חַי־יְהוָ֔ה כַּאֲשֶׁ֤ר לִמְּדוּ֙ אֶת־עַמִּ֔י לְהִשָּׁבֵ֖עַ בַּבָּ֑עַל וְנִבְנ֖וּ בְּת֥וֹךְ עַמִּֽי׃
records.gloss: And it will be, if surely they learn the ways of my people, to swear by my name, [by the] life of Yahweh, just as they taught my people to swear by Baal, then they will be built up in [the] midst of my people.
pieces: And if they will truly learn the ways of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people, swearing by {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name, "As surely as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} lives," as they themselves once taught {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people to swear by Baal, they will be built up in the midst of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people.

L.16: And it will be, if they truly learn the ways of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people, to swear by {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name, "[As] {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} lives," just as they taught {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people to swear by Baal, then they will be built up in [the] midst of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people.

R.16: Those nations once taught {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people to make promises in the name of Baal. But they may truly learn the ways of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people and make promises in {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name, saying, "As surely as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} lives." If they do, they will be built up and given a place among {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people.

decisions.choice: swear by my name, "As the LORD lives": the oath of those who worship the LORD
decisions.reason: To take an oath in God's name was to own him as one's God (4:2; 5:2; Deuteronomy 6:13). The neighbors once led Israel to swear by Baal, the Canaanite storm god; now they may learn to swear by the LORD.

decisions.choice: built up in the midst of my people: the second half of Jeremiah's call
decisions.reason: "Build" is the verb of 1:10 ("to build and to plant"). Nations that once harmed Israel may be given a secure place among God's people (compare Isaiah 56:6-7).

decisions.choice: if they truly learn
decisions.reason: The verb is doubled for emphasis: if they really learn, wholeheartedly.

decisions.choice: the past teaching put first; "make promises" for swearing; "given a place"
decisions.reason: Readable tells what the nations once did before what they may now do, says "make promises" for taking an oath, and explains "built up" as being given a place.

records.source: וְאִ֖ם לֹ֣א יִשְׁמָ֑עוּ וְנָ֨תַשְׁתִּ֜י אֶת־הַגּ֥וֹי הַה֛וּא נָת֥וֹשׁ וְאַבֵּ֖ד נְאֻם־יְהוָֽה׃ס
records.gloss: But if they will not listen, then I will uproot that nation, uprooting and destroying, declares Yahweh.
pieces: But if they will not listen, I will uproot that nation, uprooting it and destroying it completely, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

L.17: But if they will not listen, then I will uproot that nation, uprooting and destroying [it], declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

R.17: But if any nation will not obey, I will uproot it and destroy it completely, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

decisions.choice: listen: heed and obey
decisions.reason: "Listen" in Jeremiah regularly means to take God's word to heart and do it (7:23-24; 11:3-4).

decisions.choice: uprooting and destroying: complete removal
decisions.reason: The two verb forms after the main verb make it emphatic: that nation will be pulled out altogether. Like verse 14, this takes up the words of Jeremiah's call (1:10).

decisions.choice: obey ... any nation
decisions.reason: Readable says "obey" for the sense of "listen" (see m1) and "any nation" for "that nation", meaning whichever nation refuses.
